I’ll read the continuation note, check the project’s established results and controls, and use those to define the calculation and its stopping point. I’ll keep the progress record, research notes, and chat history in the investigation’s folders.

The earlier gap work already bounded center motion using narrow root intervals valid throughout the time span. For this test, I’m withholding those intervals and the final ordinates. The prediction will start from the time-zero pair, and a direct calculation from the same source will check how tightly it locates each zero.

The exact control exposed a limit of the starting data. Two polynomial heat flows can agree on both starting positions and velocities, yet their centers differ by \(567t^2+O(t^3)\) in magnitude. I’m now testing whether one fixed observation beyond the canonical pair can bound that missing acceleration and predict both positions.

Both predictions passed their accuracy tests. Using the fixed exterior observation, the final interval widths were \(1.574\times10^{-10}\) and \(8.466\times10^{-11}\) or smaller. A separate replay reproduced the numbers, and direct bisection placed each zero strictly inside both predictions.

**Both marked zeros moved to smaller Newman heights.** Starting from independently verified positions and velocities at time zero, a fixed exterior observation at height \(43.5\), together with zero counts and sign checks, gave the following certified predictions. The calculation used no later measurement at either moving zero. [Fixed-probe proof](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-6/05_arithmetic_gap_continuation/02_spatial_tensor_zero_spacings/notes/12_AGC_ST_Z_E06_FIXED_EXTERIOR_PROBE_20261120.md)

| Zero | Predicted position at \(t=10^{-4}\), rounded outward |
|---|---|
| Lower | \([28.26939232043036,\ 28.26939232058772]\) |
| Upper | \([42.04400377805427,\ 42.04400377813893]\) |

The pair’s center moved by approximately \(-0.0000667312\). Both zeros had positive acceleration throughout the interval, so each finished above the position predicted by its initial tangent.

A second forecast using source derivatives on the two root paths narrowed the respective interval widths to \(2.095\times10^{-12}\) and \(5.798\times10^{-12}\). Direct bisection from the same source reached \(2^{-54}\) per root. A separate internal reviewer reproduced both forecasts and verified that each direct bracket lay strictly inside both predictions. The fixed observation therefore establishes what exterior information suffices on this pair. Direct bisection gave the best accuracy.
